facts.heading: Daniel burned out October
facts.content: Daniel is a project manager burned out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October

facts.heading: Daniel sleeps four hours
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to Leeds
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to neurology appointments in Leeds.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about fatigue
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for being tired while his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill

facts.heading: Daniel hides fatigue from sister
facts.content: Daniel tells his sister Hannah he is fine despite being tired.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine

facts.heading: Daniel sits in car park
facts.content: Daniel sits in the hospital car park for ten minutes before entering.
facts.evidence: some days I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes

facts.heading: GP diagnosed stress and exhaustion
facts.content: Daniel's GP found normal blood tests and attributed his condition to stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Daniel refused therapy initially
facts.content: Daniel told his GP he did not have time to talk to someone.
facts.evidence: I said I hadn't got time

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire booked Daniel's session
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire booked a therapy session for him because she was tired of watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire.

facts.heading: Claire makes tea for Daniel
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire makes him tea and does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel if he wanted to go away for the weekend because he always says no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend, because I always say no.

facts.heading: Daniel refuses weekend trips
facts.content: Daniel always says no when asked to go away for the weekend.
facts.evidence: because I always say no

facts.heading: Daniel fears 200 emails while away
facts.content: Daniel worries that if he is away he will receive two hundred emails.
facts.evidence: If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them.

facts.heading: Daniel worries about his father
facts.content: Daniel worries that his father might need something if he is away.
facts.evidence: And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Daniel stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running ten kilometres every Saturday morning about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago.

facts.heading: Daniel felt his legs felt like lead
facts.content: Daniel reported that his legs felt like lead when he stopped running.
facts.evidence: My legs felt like lead

facts.heading: Daniel feels like he lost a part of himself
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself since he stopped running.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself.

facts.heading: Daniel ran for six years
facts.content: Daniel ran ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years before October.
facts.evidence: I'd done it for six years.

facts.heading: Daniel works for Peterson
facts.content: Daniel's boss is named Peterson.
facts.evidence: Peterson.

facts.heading: Peterson sends emails at night
facts.content: Daniel's boss Peterson sends emails at eleven at night.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at eleven at night

facts.heading: Daniel answers Peterson's emails immediately
facts.content: Daniel answers Peterson's emails every time, even if he is in bed.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Claire dislikes Daniel answering emails late
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire hates it when Daniel answers emails late.
facts.evidence: Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Daniel fears being fired
facts.content: Daniel fears that Peterson will let him go due to a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Daniel has a mortgage
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week
facts.content: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and went to the toilets for ten minutes.
facts.evidence: I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Daniel had heart palpitations last week
facts.content: Daniel's heart was going and his hands were shaking last week when he snapped at a colleague.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Daniel had panic attack on train
facts.content: Daniel had a panic attack on the train to Manchester and had to get off to stand on the platform.
facts.evidence: Once on the train to Manchester. I just had to get off and stand on the platform.

facts.heading: Daniel hasn't told anyone about panic
facts.content: Daniel has not told anyone about the panic attack, not even Claire.
facts.evidence: I haven't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Daniel worries he is losing it
facts.content: Daniel believes the panic attack means he is losing it and will not be able to cope.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Daniel drinks six cups of coffee daily
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: Coffee, probably. I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Daniel drinks wine to switch off
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off, having two glasses sometimes three.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Daniel feels uneasy about drinking wine
facts.content: Daniel feels uneasy about the wine because it only works for an hour and he wakes at three anyway.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway. I know it's not helping.

facts.heading: Daniel feels relief from talking
facts.content: Daniel felt strange and relieved after talking about his issues, like putting down a bag he didn't realize he was carrying.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Daniel wants to put down the nights
facts.content: Daniel wants to put down the nights, believing that if he could sleep he could cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Daniel's grandfather worked in Yorkshire mines
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire and never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once.

facts.heading: Daniel's father is like his grandfather
facts.content: Daniel's father is like his grandfather; they both just get on with things without complaining.
facts.evidence: Dad's the same. You just get on with it.

facts.heading: Daniel feels he is like his father
facts.content: Daniel feels he is the same as his grandfather and father, thinking they would think he is weak for being in therapy.
facts.evidence: I'm the same. I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Daniel says he is not weak
facts.content: Daniel says he is not weak, just very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Daniel plans to stop using phone at 9:30
facts.content: Daniel plans to switch off his phone at half past nine for twenty minutes.
facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Daniel plans to write a note about the night
facts.content: Daniel plans to write down when he wakes up if he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I can do that. I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Daniel feels tired but lighter
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after talking about his issues.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.

facts.heading: Daniel will attend next week
facts.content: Daniel plans to attend the next therapy session on time.
facts.evidence: I'll try to make it on time
